original_question: Kapustin's restriction is equivalent to the condition integral log |theta| > -infinity. Does that analytic condition admit an interpretation purely in spectral terms?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem in the paper’s discussion of non-inner characteristic functions / Clark theory: whether Kapustin’s extra hypothesis on the scalar characteristic function theta admits a characterization purely in spectral terms.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies that the target is a Kapustin-related open question from the rank-one unitary perturbation / Clark-theory part of the paper, and that the substance of the question is to reinterpret an analytic hypothesis on theta in spectral language.
missing_details: The paper is not asking about an arbitrary function theta; theta is the scalar characteristic function of the completely nonunitary contraction arising in the rank-one unitary perturbation setting.

The analytic condition is not simply integral log|theta| > -infinity. In this context the relevant condition is the non-extreme / Szego condition, equivalently the integrability of the logarithm of the defect: integral over T of log(1-|theta(ξ)|^2) dm(ξ) > -infinity (equivalently integral log Delta > -infinity with Delta=(1-|theta|^2)^(1/2)).
The ambient domain and measure need to be specified: theta is analytic contractive on the unit disk, boundary values are taken on the unit circle T, and m is normalized Lebesgue measure on T.

The question is about a spectral interpretation in the rank-one perturbation sense: namely in terms of the spectral data of the associated family of unitary rank-one perturbations / Aleksandrov-Clark measures, not just the bare point spectrum of a single operator.
The draft does not say that Kapustin’s restriction is an additional hypothesis used in the non-inner characteristic-function discussion of the paper.
The draft does not make explicit that the paper is asking for a characterization/interpretation, not for a new broader generalization.
The draft omits the standard name of the condition ('non-extreme' or 'Szego condition'), which is needed to make the question stand alone and faithful to the paper’s intent.
refined_question: In the paper’s rank-one unitary perturbation / Clark-theory setting, let theta be the scalar characteristic function of the associated completely nonunitary contraction, with theta a Schur-class function on the unit disk. Kapustin imposes the additional assumption that theta be non-extreme, equivalently that its defect function Delta=(1-|theta|^2)^(1/2) satisfy the Szego condition integral over T of log Delta dm > -infinity (equivalently integral over T of log(1-|theta(ξ)|^2) dm(ξ) > -infinity). Does this additional hypothesis admit a characterization purely in spectral terms, i.e. directly from the spectral data of the associated rank-one unitary perturbations / Aleksandrov-Clark measures?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: can one characterize, purely from the Aleksandrov-Clark spectral measures associated with theta, when theta is non-extreme (or satisfies the Szego condition integral over T of log(1-|theta(ξ)|^2) dm(ξ) > -infinity)?
justification: The draft clearly does not target the self-adjoint finite-rank part of the survey; the Kapustin reference and the logarithmic integrability condition place it in the later discussion of non-inner characteristic functions and Clark theory. In that part of the paper, the relevant extra hypothesis is the standard non-extreme/Szego condition for the scalar characteristic function, and the natural paper-faithful sharpening is to ask whether that hypothesis can be read off from the spectral side of the associated rank-one perturbation family. The main correction needed is the analytic formula itself: the paper’s condition is on the defect 1-|theta|^2 (or its square root Delta), not on |theta| alone.
